```{r setup}
# Libraries
source("scripts/config.R")

# Load the current geographic analysis and its three result objects.
source("scripts/geography_analysis.R")

required <- c("zip_result", "tracts_result", "neighborhood_result")
missing_results <- required[!vapply(required, exists, logical(1), inherits = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_results)) {
  stop("Missing result objects: ", paste(missing_results, collapse = ", "),
       ". Source your geographic analysis script in the setup chunk.")
}

results <- list(
  "ZIP/ZCTA" = zip_result,
  "Census tract" = tracts_result,
  "Neighborhood Statistical Area" = neighborhood_result
)
```

## Geographic coverage comparison

The table compares restaurant coverage, geographic area sizes, restaurant counts,
and restaurant density for the selected vegetarian-friendly categories: "Vegetarian", "Vegan", "Falafel", "Bagels".

All measures come from each result's `geo_system_summary` and `area_summat` table.

**Matched restaurants** fall within a boundary in the geographic system.
**Unmatched restaurants** have coordinates but fall outside all boundaries;
restaurants with **missing coordinates** are counted separately.
**Total unassigned** is the sum of those last two groups. Restaurant-count
statistics exclude areas with zero restaurants. Density is measured in
restaurants per square mile and likewise excludes zero-restaurant areas.

```{r comparison-table}
comparison_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(results), function(label) {
  summary <- results[[label]]$geo_system_summary |>
    st_drop_geometry()

  tibble(
    `Geographic system` = label,

    # Restaurant coverage
    `Total restaurants` = summary$total_restaurants,
    `Missing coordinates` = summary$restaurants_w_missing_coord,
    `Matched restaurants` = summary$matched_restaurants,
    `Unmatched restaurants` = summary$unmatched_restaurants,
    

    # Boundary coverage and size
    `Total areas` = summary$total_areas,
    `Areas with restaurants` = summary$total_areas - summary$empty_areas,
    `Empty areas` = summary$empty_areas,
    `Sparse areas` = summary$sparse_areas,
    `Mean area (sq mi)` = summary$avg_sqmi,
    `Median area (sq mi)` = summary$median_sqmi,

    # Restaurant counts in non-empty areas
    `Minimum restaurants per area` = summary$min_restaurants,
    `25th percentile restaurants per area` = summary$q25_restaurants,
    `Median restaurants per area` = summary$median_restaurants,
    `Mean restaurants per area` = summary$mean_restaurants,
    `75th percentile restaurants per area` = summary$q75_restaurants,
    `Maximum restaurants per area` = summary$max_restaurants,

    # Density in non-empty areas
    `Minimum density` = summary$min_density,
    `25th percentile density` = summary$q25_density,
    `Median density` = summary$median_density,
    `Mean density` = summary$mean_density,
    `75th percentile density` = summary$q75_density,
    `Maximum density` = summary$max_density
  )
}))

# Display metrics down the rows for a readable, side-by-side comparison.
count_metrics <- c(
  "Total restaurants", "Missing coordinates", "Matched restaurants", "Unmatched restaurants",
   "Total areas", "Areas with restaurants", "Empty areas", "Sparse areas"
  , "Minimum restaurants per area"
  , "25th percentile restaurants per area"
  , "Median restaurants per area"
  , "75th percentile restaurants per area"
  , "Maximum restaurants per area", "Areas below median density"
)

comparison_display <- comparison_table |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -`Geographic system`,
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Category = case_when(
      Metric %in% c("Total restaurants", "Matched restaurants",
                    "Unmatched restaurants", "Missing coordinates") ~ "Restaurant coverage",
      Metric %in% c("Total areas", "Areas with restaurants", "Empty areas", "Sparse areas",
                    "Mean area (sq mi)", "Median area (sq mi)") ~ "Geographic areas",
      str_detect(Metric, "restaurants per area") ~ "Restaurants per area",
      TRUE ~ "Restaurant density (per sq mi)"
    ),
    Value = if_else(
      Metric %in% count_metrics,
      formatC(Value, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ","),
      formatC(Value, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ",")
    )
  ) |>
  select(Category, Metric, `Geographic system`, Value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = `Geographic system`, values_from = Value)

knitr::kable(
  comparison_display,
  caption = "Geographic coverage, area size, restaurant counts, and density by system",
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

## Area summary (more than 3 restaurants)

Each tab contains every area with `n_restaurants > 3` in that geographic system.
Scroll horizontally to see all metrics; the **Geographic system** and **Area name**
columns remain fixed. Scroll vertically to view long tables; there is no row pagination.

```{r area-summary-data}
area_summary_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(results), function(label) {
  results[[label]]$area_summary |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    filter(n_restaurants > 3) |>
    transmute(
      `Geographic system` = label,
      `Area name` = area_name,
      Restaurants = n_restaurants,
      `Area (sq mi)` = round(area_sqmi, 2),
      `Restaurants / sq mi` = round(restaurants_per_sqmi, 2),
      `Average rating` = round(avg_rating, 2),
      `Median rating` = round(median_rating, 2),
      `Weighted rating` = round(weighted_rating, 2)
    )
})) |>
  arrange(`Geographic system`, desc(Restaurants), `Area name`)

# FixedColumns freezes the first two columns while the remaining metrics scroll.
make_area_table <- function(geography) {
  DT::datatable(
    area_summary_table |>
      filter(`Geographic system` == geography),
    rownames = FALSE,
    extensions = 'FixedColumns',
    options = list(
      scrollX = TRUE,
      scrollY = "550px",
      scrollCollapse = TRUE,
      fixedColumns = list(leftColumns = 2),
      paging = FALSE,
      searching = TRUE,
      info = FALSE,
      dom = 'ft'
    )
  )
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### 1. ZIP/ZCTA

```{r area-summary-zip}
make_area_table("ZIP/ZCTA")
```

### 2. Census tract

```{r area-summary-tracts}
make_area_table("Census tract")
```

### 3. Neighborhood Statistical Area

```{r area-summary-neighborhood}
make_area_table("Neighborhood Statistical Area")
```

:::

## Restaurant locations by geographic area

All three maps use the same longitude and latitude limits. Gray polygons show
geographic boundaries, and dark-blue points show restaurant locations with
valid coordinates. Point color does not represent restaurant counts or density.

```{r}
#| label: geographic-maps
#| column: screen
#| out-width: 90%
#| fig-cap: "Restaurant locations by geographic system, using a shared map extent."

make_map <- function(result, title) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf_interactive(
      data = result$area_summary,
      aes(
        fill = n_restaurants > 3,
        tooltip = paste0(
          area_name,
          "\nRestaurants: ", n_restaurants
        )
      ),
      color = "grey60",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "FALSE" = "gray90",
        "TRUE" = "#d4ebf2"
      ),
      labels = c("0–3", "4+"),
      name = "Number of Restaurants"
    ) +
    geom_sf(
      data = result$restaurants,
      color = "darkblue",
      alpha = 0.5,
      size = 0.7
    ) +
    coord_sf(
      xlim = c(-90.2, -90.0),
      ylim = c(29.9, 30.05),
      default_crs = st_crs(4326),
      expand = FALSE
    ) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_minimal()
}

maps <- Map(make_map, results, names(results))

combined_maps <- wrap_plots(maps, ncol = 3) +
  plot_layout(
    guides = "collect",
    axes = "collect_y"
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8)
  )

girafe(
  ggobj = combined_maps,
  width_svg = 12,
  height_svg = 4.8
)
```
